lines.text: How often they disobeyed Him in the wilderness
and grieved Him in the desert!
Again and again they tested God
and provoked the Holy One of Israel.
They did not remember His power—
the day He redeemed them from the adversary,
when He performed His signs in Egypt
and His wonders in the fields of Zoan.
He turned their rivers to blood,
and from their streams they could not drink.
He sent swarms of flies that devoured them,
He gave their crops to the grasshopper,
the fruit of their labor to the locust.
He killed their vines with hailstones
He abandoned their cattle to the hail
and their livestock to bolts of lightning.

pictures.scene: Edward Lear, Masada on the Dead Sea — the rock fortress over the dead water with nothing living around it, how often they disobeyed Him in the wilderness, and grieved Him in the desert
pictures.name: pd_lear_masada_dead_sea

pictures.scene: Jan Both, Italiaans landschap met overzetveer — the ferry going over and coming back across the same water, again and again they tested God, and provoked the Holy One of Israel
pictures.name: pd_both_italiaans_landschap_overzetveer

pictures.scene: Konstantin Savitsky, Repair Work on the Railway — the gang bent to the embankment carrying the earth basket by basket, they did not remember His power, the day He redeemed them from the adversary
pictures.name: pd_savitsky_repair_work_railway

pictures.scene: David Roberts, Portico of the Temple of Edfu — the great temple of Egypt with its columns standing where they were raised, when He performed His signs in Egypt, and His wonders in the fields of Zoan
pictures.name: pd_roberts_portico_edfu

pictures.scene: Lieve Verschuier, The Great Fire of London — the whole river turned the colour of the fire burning along it, He turned their rivers to blood, and from their streams they could not drink
pictures.name: pd_verschuier_fire_of_london

pictures.scene: Otto Marseus van Schrieck, Planten en insekten — the creeping and flying things come out thick over the undergrowth, He sent swarms of flies that devoured them, and frogs that devastated them
pictures.name: pd_marseus_planten_en_insekten

pictures.scene: Pieter Brueghel the Younger, The Tax Collector's Office — the year's increase written down and taken away by other hands, He gave their crops to the grasshopper, the fruit of their labor to the locust
pictures.name: pd_brueghel_tax_collectors_office

pictures.scene: Andreas Achenbach, Landschaft mit Fluss — the trees taken by the weather and the river running hard beneath them, He killed their vines with hailstones, and their sycamore-figs with sleet
pictures.name: pd_achenbach_landschaft_mit_fluss

pictures.scene: Anton Mauve, Koe — the cow standing alone out in the open field with no cover over it, He abandoned their cattle to the hail, and their livestock to bolts of lightning
pictures.name: pd_mauve_koe
